MX17 re-run plan

The from-scratch re-run of the cosmic-bench and SPS analysis (plan, 2026-10-23)

Goal (Dylan, 2026-10-23): one complete, consistent pass of every June cosmic-bench and SPS det4 analysis, on lxplus condor, with the physical detector model, producing every number and figure of the two detector papers. n_TOF is out of scope for these papers. The pass should run once, so everything that would force it to run again is settled first. This file is the plan; CHECKS_2026-10-23.md is the record of the checks behind it.

0 · Decisions taken

decision (2026-10-23)
Kernel The physical RC kernel (wft.model.build_matrix_rc): prompt footprint σ0 per view, RC spread along the resistive strips (D_rc, Y only), drift diffusion; no fitted copy amplitudes. Supersedes the 10-23 morning note "C2 = freeze r06".
X asymmetry Not modelled; wft.xasym is a ± systematic (XASYM_CONTINGENCY.md). Toy cost: −0.05° overall, ∓0.19° head-on.
Inputs Keep EOS decoded_root, combined_hits_root and M3 v2 rays where a fresh decode of a sample reproduces them; re-decode what does not.
Where lxplus condor only. Outputs on EOS; AFS holds code and logs only.
Scope All June bench rows (golden long runs, HV scans, det3 drift scan), all SPS det4 runs, timing on waveforms. The hits-vs-waveforms comparison (Paper II R1–R5) is a side project at the end, on comparison datasets only.
Datasets Golden runs set the calibrations and the quoted numbers; the other runs are consistency checks, read skeptically where a run is known to be bad (§5).

1 · What forces a re-run, and what does not

Only upstream choices force the full pass to be repeated: the inputs (decode, hits for seeding, M3/uRWELL reference), every calibration constant in a bundle, the reconstruction settings (waveform preparation, depth grid, solver, seeding) and the alignment. Everything downstream of the reconstructed tables — stacks, gas fits, D_T, efficiency definitions, timing, maps, figures — can be iterated after the pass for the cost of a script. The pre-run work below is therefore about the upstream list; the downstream questions (§6) are worked during and after the pass.

4 · Stages of the pass

stage what gate before the next stage
S0 Re-decode + re-hit the June rows; decode SPS FEU 03; matched lists for every row; inventory every row has decoded, hits and reference; counts logged against the old ones
S1 Calibrate each chamber on its golden calibration run (W1–W6, W11, W12), with the iteration gate table on the golden evaluation run: resolution, bias, slope, implied-v flatness, efficiency, χ²; v against timing and Magboltz
S2 Reconstruct every row with its per-condition bundle (W7), one job per (row, file) completion ledger, no row missing
S3 Alignment → efficiency → angles → maps → digest, per row the digest reproduces S1's gate on the golden rows
S4 Detector characterization: v(E) and gas, gap, D_T, D_rc, σ0, attachment, gain and HV curves, sparks, charge balance, timing on waveforms (D3), edge tilt (D4), X asymmetry; SPS: kernel, spatial resolution on the waveform fit (centroid as the cross-check), known-angle test at 25.6° (R7) each result reproduces its pre-run value or the difference is explained in writing
S5 Consistency checks on the non-golden runs a table per chamber
S6 Paper figures and numbers from papers/*/figures.toml; reports every \requote replaced
S7 Side project: hits vs waveforms (R1–R5) on the comparison datasets —

Rough cost: W1–W12 a few working days (W1/W12 and W9/W10 are the large ones); S0–S3 one to two days of condor; S4–S6 about a week.

6 · Downstream questions (do not block the pass; worked in S4)

  • det3's X diffusion excess (+160…+260 µm/√cm) — re-measure with the masked common mode and a full-column selection.
  • Water per chamber and night; det6 slower than det7 on the same night.
  • Three-body O₂ attachment scale (beam).
  • det4's X under the RC kernel (+0.06…+0.16° against production).
  • The X asymmetry's mechanism (closed unexplained).

7 · Stated limitations (no new data)

The detectors are gone. Anything not answerable from the existing data, simulation or the literature is written down as a limitation: the asymmetry mechanism, the resistive-strip mask, the τ and c2 tails beyond the SPS window, a dry-gas bench run, Stephan's unanswered geometry questions, det6's window-limited deep charge.

8 · Decisions on the open questions (Dylan, 2026-10-23 evening)

  1. Re-decode every June row with one decoder, after an audit that the decoder is now correct; audit the M3 decoding/tracking chain the same way.
  2. Analysis first. Quote from the largest-statistics runs if they show no problem; fall back to other runs if they do.
  3. Diffusion: per-chamber measured Dp (Magboltz as the comparison), but its consistency across chambers and runs is a result to be checked; if the measurements disagree, write it up as a limit of our understanding with an error bar, not hide it.
  4. det6: full analysis, every number produced; what to quote is decided at writing time (det6 is known poor).
  5. C8: redo the calibration fully with the reference position from the waveforms. C9: investigate the common mode thoroughly and build the correction into the analysis.

C8 · The calibration's reference position biases v — CONFIRMED on det3 (fleet running)

First C7 results (K = 18, σ0_x pinned 0.25): v = 41.2 (det2), 42.1 (det3), 25.3 (det6), 37.7 (det7) µm/ns. det3's 42.1 is above dry Magboltz at its field (38.5) and 20 % above what free fits read under the same kernel (§12: slope 0.96 at 36.6 → 35 µm/ns); det6 stays 33 % below det7 on the same night and field.

Cause: the ref-pinned objective fixes p0 at ref_mesh, the M3 track at the plane the hits-chain alignment (alignment_tpc_veto50, wft.calibrate line ~63) placed the detector. Hit times are compressed 20–30 % (RECONSTRUCTION_BASIS.md), so that plane is biased, and a depth offset is absorbed as dv ≈ dz / ⟨drift time⟩.

Test (rerun/precheck_vscan/v_scan.py, det3, 60 calibration events, RC constants of the rcv25 fit fixed, recal.py's cold objective):

p0 χ² at the minimum v at the minimum
pinned at ref_mesh (calibration as run) 4.60e7 39.6
profiled ±1 mm (recal.py --p0-profile) 3.07e7 (−34 %) 37.0

→ W1 changes: the reference geometry used for calibration must not come from the hits alignment. Calibrate with p0 profiled, run the reco, align on the waveform positions (mx_june_wft/01_alignment.py), and if a pinned calibration is wanted, rebuild ref_mesh from that alignment and iterate until v is stable. Every bundle made so far, r06 included, was calibrated against the hits-based reference. Fleet: condor 4538813 (det2, det3 K24, det6 and det7 at K 18 and 24).

C9 · The reconstruction's common mode moves with the signal — fix written (opt-in), validation pending

wft.io subtracts the plain per-sample median of each 64-channel block. On det7 (6-26, 495 V, FEU 08, 4000 events) the track clusters are ~17 strips wide, and against a median that masks the cluster ±3 strips:

strips of the block masked baseline error at the pulse peak, median / p90 largest error in the window, median
1–8 0 / 3.5 ADC 3.5 ADC
8–20 2.5 / 15 ADC 9–10 ADC
20–40 4 / 51 ADC 104 ADC

Under 1 % of a ~4000 ADC peak, but applied to every strip of the block: 10–25 % of a neighbour's tail, which is what the RC kernel's σ0 and D_rc, and the D_T stacks, are measured from. cloud_basics' stacks used a masked common mode; the reconstruction never did. Fix: wft.io.masked_block_median, opt-in WFT_CM_MASK=<half-width> (default 0 = bit-identical), reference-free two-pass median; on a toy (30-strip track in one block) the baseline error on the quiet strips goes from −16 to −1.3 ADC. → W11: rebuild the golden calibration caches with it and gate it (resolution, χ², σ0, D_rc) before the freeze.

C10 · Common mode, investigated (2026-10-23 evening, laptop; rerun/cm_study/)

Where the common mode is removed. Every June production row was taken RAW: run_config has zero_suppress, pedestal_subtraction and common_noise_subtraction all False (only the pre-June ArIso/ZS test runs had on-FEU CM). The decoder does no baseline work (DreamDecoder.cpp read through). So the CM is removed only in software, in two places, both the plain per-sample median of each 64-channel block (= one DREAM chip = one connector): the hits analyzer (applyCommonNoiseSubtraction, also used for the pedestal RMS) and wft.io. Nothing is baked into the data: the CM can be redone in the analysis at no cost.

What the CM is (cm_structure.py, golden files, signal-free events):

FEU raw noise → after CM (ADC) CM rms per chip chip CM left after the FEU-wide CM X–Y CM correlation
det7 X (06) / Y (08) 59 → 8.3 / 53 → 9.0 50–65 (X chip 0: 5) 9–20 −0.46
det6 X (03) / Y (04) 136 → 8.0 / 142 → 8.7 132–146 12–20 −0.89
  • It changes sample to sample (within-event rms ≈ total), so it has to be estimated per sample.
  • Most of it is FEU-wide, but each chip keeps 9–20 ADC of its own, more than the noise (8–9): quiet chips cannot stand in for a chip that holds a track.
  • The X and Y FEUs of one detector are anti-correlated.
  • Per-channel pick-up is uniform to ±5–15 % (slope p1–p99 0.9–1.15 apart from dead channels); a per-channel slope lowers the noise only 8.05 → 7.78 ADC. Not worth a model term.
  • det7 X chip 0 carries almost no CM (5 against ~60 ADC), as if its strips were not connected to the detector. Open: check against the dead-strip masks.

What the plain median does to a track (cm_inject.py): real clusters (cleaned with a ±10-strip masked CM, zero outside) injected into real signal-free events of the same file, 1000–1200 per plane, all five chambers, both views; error = E(quiet + signal) − E(quiet), which isolates the signal-induced part. Median bias on the window-integrated charge of the ±k neighbours:

estimator ±1, ±2 ±3 ±5
plain median (production) −0.2 … −2.5 % −0.5 … −6 % −1 … −25 % (narrow clusters worst)
masked, ±5 strips (WFT_CM_MASK=5) ≤ 0.1 % ≤ 0.3 % ≤ 1 %

The masked estimator also has the smaller random error (|ΔQ±3| p90 roughly halved). Mask half-widths 2–8 behave the same; 5 is chosen. A fallback to the FEU-wide CM for a fully covered chip changes nothing measurable (too rare). Correction to C9: the "10–25 % of a neighbour's tail" there compared two estimators on the same event (it includes the masked estimator's own noise); isolated by injection, the plain-median bias is the table above: small near the core, large in the far tail, which is where D_rc and the diffusion width are measured.

The hits analyzer: --cns-mask M added to analyze_waveforms (mm_strip_reconstruction, same rule as wft.io); --cns-mask 0 is bit-identical to the production hits (det7 golden file 000, FEU 06 and 08). With M = 5 the hit count rises 18 % (X) / 24 % (Y), mostly 1–5 channels from a cluster (cluster edges the biased baseline had pushed under threshold). Whether the re-hit adopts it is a decision (hits are seeding, efficiency and QA, not geometry).

C11 · Decoder audit and full June re-decode — PASS (condor 4543155/4543157, rerun/decoder_audit/)

What was run. Every .fdf of the 100 June-manifest subruns (1278 files: data and pedestal, MX17 FEUs and the M3 FEU 01, 102 GB) was re-decoded with the pinned decoder (fa80c06; the 36eb894 build's DreamDecoder.cpp is byte-identical) into <subrun>/decoded_root_fa80c06/ next to the old decoded_root/ (left untouched), and audited in the same job:

  • audit_decode.py decodes the .fdf a second time, independently: numpy on the 16-bit word stream, written from the word format (dreamdataline.h) and not from DreamDecoder.cpp's control flow. Events = runs of frames with one eventID. Compared event by event with the C++ output: eventId, timestamp, ftst, word count and two position-weighted 64-bit hashes of (sample, channel, amplitude). Negative control: one amplitude changed by one ADC is caught.
  • It also checks the format itself: FEU header lengths, DREAM block lengths, the word after each trailer, padding, repeated sample indices, blocks per frame.

Consequences.

  • The decoder is right, and the June dataset now has one decoder provenance. The M3 rays (DataReader v2, 7-05) are consistent with the new decodes and need no re-tracking.
  • Incomplete events are flagged per file (decode_audit/<run>/<subrun>/<file>.npz, complete), wft.io skips them (FeuReader.incomplete), and efficiency must take them out of the denominator ("not measured"), not count them as misses: ≤ 0.23 % of events, ≤ 0.012 % of rays.
  • Two bugs found in the old hits driver (reprocess_cosmic_bench.py), both only on det3_test 6-22 short_run (two acquisitions in one subrun): files grouped by file number alone (15H51_000 and 15H55_000 collide in the combine) and one pedestal used for both acquisitions. The re-hit groups by date_time_fnum and matches the pedestal by stamp.

C13 · M3 chain re-audited; hits common mode decided on data (2026-10-23 night, rerun/m3_audit/)

Judge (judge.py): independent of M3's own χ². Every clean M3 ray (NClus ≥ 3 both views, 0 < χ² < 5, one per event) is projected to the detector; the detector's largest-charge cluster per view (combined hits, hot channels

20 % occupancy dropped) is tied to it by an affine fit per view on the baseline rays with the plain-CM hits, then frozen. Read inside the footprint: match = cluster within 5 mm in both views; residual width (1.4826 × MAD). Rays a variant adds are scored separately. Golden files: det6/det7 6-26 long_run 000/005, det3 Saturday 000–003, det3 weekend 01H34 000/004, det4 6-24 000/003, det2/det3 6-22 longer_run 000/001.

M3 provenance. All 181 June M3 acquisitions have v2 rays (DataReader/tracking of 7-05, config_ref_june2026, pedestal of their own subrun or night). Source changes since: b71ffc9 (8-25) adds output branches only; akallitss's fork adds configs/CI/docs only. A clean rebuild reproduces the production rays exactly on all 12 golden files (event order differs: the tracking is multi-threaded; compare keyed on evn).

The algorithm, read again. 61 channels → 1037 strips by genetic multiplexing per plane; channels > 4σ for > 3 samples; cluster = longest run of strips whose channels fired; charge-weighted centroid with shared channels split; plain per-chip median CM; track = minimum-χ² combination over the 4 layers, a layer dropped only if no 4-layer combination has χ²/n < 200 mm². Two candidate improvements were written (opt-in, off = bit-identical, verified on the 12 files) and judged:

variant clean rays match (det3 Sat.) what the added rays do
production 19 691 91.3 %, σ 0.80/0.75 mm —
outlier rescue (M3_OUTLIER_CHI2=5: a failing 4-layer fit replaced by its best 3-layer subset) +27 % 84.1 % match 58–65 %, σ 1.1 mm: mostly worse or fake tracks; rejected
masked CM in M3 (M3_CM_MASK=0/1) ±2 % swapped 91.2–91.3 % no change in match or σ on any chamber (a track lights 3–6 of 64 channels); not needed

Same picture on det2, det4, det6, det7 and the det3 weekend. The production M3 rays stand; no re-tracking.

Hits common mode: plain median (rr1_cm0). Same judge, production rays, plain vs masked-CM hits:

chamber plain (cm0) masked (cm5)
det6 90.0 % 78.1 %
det7 69.5 % 39.0 %
det3 Sat. / weekend / 6-22 91.3 / 91.5 / 92.6 % 90.5 / 90.5 / 91.8 %
det2 89.8 % 89.3 %
det4 53.4 % 52.8 %

Residual widths do not change. Cause, found in the waveforms: in sparks and whole-chip saturations (det7: chip median ~3700 ADC) the plain median cancels the coherent shift and the track cluster survives, while the median of the unmasked channels leaves up to ±900 ADC on every strip, which becomes the largest cluster. The masked CM's gain (the far tails) matters only to the waveform fit, not to the hits.

wft.io masked CM: coherent-event guard added (CM_GUARD = 3): the masked median is used for a chip only if the unmasked channels' spread around it is below 3 × the chip's noise; otherwise the plain median. Falls back on 6.3 % of masked chips on det7 6-26, 0.9 % on det3 Saturday. Test added. W11 still has to gate it on the fit (sparks are vetoed in the reconstruction, so the guard should rarely matter there).

C16 · W1/W12 calibration iteration — the planned loop does not converge; protocol arms running (night of 10-24)

Iteration 0 (DAG w12/it0.dag, all five calibration rows): RECO with the W11 profiled bundle (plain CM, K 24, guard on; 4–8 k matched events) → 01_alignment on the waveform positions → calibration cache with ref_mesh from that alignment (build_cache(align_path=...)) → pinned RC fit (σ0_x, σ0_y, D_rc,y, v).

v profiled (W11, hits ref) v pinned to the waveform alignment timing v waveform − hits alignment
det2 40.9 40.2 39.3 ± 1.2 dz +3/+1 mm, dθ 0.00°, dxy ≤ 0.01 mm
det3 37.6 39.5 35.8 ± 0.6 dz +2/0 mm, dθ −0.05°
det4 34.0 41.3 33.0 ± 0.7 dz +2/+1 mm
det6 22.0 24.1 25.9 ± 0.8 dz +1/−2 mm, dθ −0.05°
det7 32.9 33.5 36.8 ± 1.1 dz +3/+1 mm

The waveform alignment differs from the hits alignment only by 1–3 mm in z (on the 1 mm scan grid) and nothing in plane, and the mesh position barely depends on v, so iterating will not move it. But a plane error Δz moves the reference position at the mesh by tan θ · Δz, which a pinned fit absorbs into v: a few mm on the 30 mm gap is a 5–20 % v error. The alignment cannot place the plane finely enough to pin the reference; the pinned v is not a calibration. The C8 statement "rebuild ref_mesh from the waveform alignment and iterate" is withdrawn.

What the calibration protocol has to be, tested overnight (w12/arms_it0.dag, same it0 caches): A = p0 profiled ±1 mm (W11's method), B = profiled ±2 mm in 0.2 mm steps, C = pinned with a global plane offset per view (dz_x, dz_y free in recal.py). A 12-event test of C ran into a v–dz valley (dz_y to its −10 mm bound): a common event-time shift trades against the mesh position, and only the drift column's ends break it. Agreement of A, B and C (and with the timing v) defines the converged calibration; disagreement is the calibration systematic.

Also fixed: the fit jobs deleted the condor scratch dir itself (exit 1, logs lost; results were written); the bundle summary printed the unused delayed-copy constants for RC bundles.

Same it0 caches (reference = waveform alignment), RC kernel, K 24, guard on, held-out events reconstructed blind (w12/arms_it0.json). v in µm/ns; s68 = held-out angle resolution X/Y in degrees.

  • With v free the methods scatter by 15–25 % (det4: A and B 27 % apart on the same cache). C runs into the v–dz valley (dz to −2…−6 mm) and gives the worst resolution on det2/3/4: rejected.
  • D (v fixed at the timing v) reaches the same or a LOWER training χ² than v free (det3 1.0894e8 vs B 1.0906e8, det4 1.3024e8 vs 1.3045e8; det2 +0.2 %, det7 +1.7 %, det6 +4 %) and the best or near-best held-out resolution on every chamber. The χ² is nearly flat along v and the free-v minimiser stops on that flat floor: the waveform fit cannot measure v; the drift column's duration over the geometric gap can.
  • The timing v itself carries 2–4 % (gap ±0.2…1.1 mm, 1.5 % on T) and is not unique: det7's longer run gives 32.8 against its long run's 36.8 (the 4σ discrepancy noted in plan §5; the profiled fits sit at 31.6–32.5).

Candidate protocol (for Dylan's decision): v from timing (cloud_basics/vdrift_consistency.py, per chamber and condition), kernel (σ0_x, σ0_y, D_rc,y) from the waveform fit with p0 profiled ±2 mm about the waveform-aligned reference, w0/kw measured under the final bundle (W6). Its convergence (kernel stable when the reference is rebuilt from a reconstruction with it) is being checked (w12/itD1.dag). The v systematic is the timing v's error and the D-vs-B spread.
